node_definition.done_when: Read section 27 of crew-observability-truth first; it names three items. First, a test drives dispatch() in dry-run form and asserts the composed prompt carries the deadline derived from launch_instant, pinning the wiring into _compose_dispatch_prompt. Second, change_lane in reckon/crew/dispatch.py restates the time fence for the new attempt when it relaunches a run from its retained prompt, as resume does, so a moved attempt reads its own deadline rather than the previous attempt's. Third, audit_manifest in reckon/crew/reports.py reports a manifest whose blocker cites an expired time fence before its recorded deadline as a defect, not a blocker. tests/test_time_fence_follows_the_attempt.py has one test per item, each failing before its change. Existing tests reaching change_lane, _compose_dispatch_prompt or audit_manifest keep passing; grep tests/ for each to build the gate. Record the outcome in docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/time-fence-follows-the-attempt.html. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line as revision= followed by the full sha, and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
